questions.question: What does the passage say is at the core of unbelief that fights against Islam?
questions.answer: It says the core is rejecting the truth, not knowing it, and saying no to it.

questions.question: How is belief described in the passage?
questions.answer: It is described as true knowledge, a real confirmation, and a sound judgment.

questions.question: If unbelief looks like it is claiming something, what is it really like according to the passage?
questions.answer: It only seems positive on the outside, but in truth it is a kind of lack and denial.

questions.question: What does the passage say each denying side of belief can hide or lead to?
questions.answer: It can cover a real truth or be a door leading to a positive truth.

questions.question: When can unbelief be counted in one way as a wrong kind of knowledge?
questions.answer: When people work hard to treat their negative view as if it were something they can accept and approve.

questions.question: What is simple refusal to accept called in the passage?
questions.answer: It is called complete ignorance and a total lack of judgment.

questions.question: How many main kinds of convictions under unbelief are mentioned?
questions.answer: Two main kinds are mentioned.

questions.question: What is the first main kind of unbelief like?
questions.answer: It does not deal with the truths of Islam directly, but holds a false belief of its own and makes an unfair judgment.

questions.question: Why is that first main kind not discussed further?
questions.answer: Because it is said not to be the subject being talked about.

questions.question: What does the second main kind of unbelief do?
questions.answer: It stands against the truths of faith and struggles with them.

questions.question: What is the first variety inside this second main kind?
questions.answer: It is just not agreeing with the truth, without making a firm judgment.

questions.question: Why is this first variety said to happen easily?
questions.answer: Because it is only ignorance and does not require a settled judgment.

questions.question: What is the second variety inside the opposing kind of unbelief?
questions.answer: It is inwardly agreeing with non-existence and taking that side.

questions.question: Why must this second variety try to support its denial?
questions.answer: Because it becomes a chosen view of the heart, so it feels bound to defend that view.

questions.question: What is the first type of negation mentioned near the end?
questions.answer: It is denying that a certain thing exists in one certain place or direction.

questions.question: Why can that first type of negation be proven?
questions.answer: Because it is limited and specific, so it can be checked.

questions.question: What is the second type of negation about?
questions.answer: It is about denying broad religious truths connected to the world, all beings, the next life, and time.

questions.question: Why can this second type not be proved?
questions.answer: Because proving it would require seeing all of creation, the hereafter, and every part of time.

questions.question: What big difference does the passage make between belief and unbelief?
questions.answer: Belief is linked to knowledge and truth, while unbelief is linked to denial and not knowing.

questions.question: Which one is connected with real existence in the passage: belief or unbelief?
questions.answer: Belief is connected with real existence.

questions.question: Why does the passage say unbelief can sometimes look like a claim or position?
questions.answer: Because a person may try to present rejection as if it were a settled view.

questions.question: What makes that kind of unbelief only a mistaken form of knowing?
questions.answer: It accepts something false and judges wrongly instead of knowing the truth.

questions.question: What is easier than building a false belief according to the passage?
questions.answer: Simply refusing to accept the truth is easier.

questions.question: What is missing when someone only refuses to accept?
questions.answer: A real judgment is missing.

questions.question: What are the two main kinds of unbelieving convictions listed in the passage?
questions.answer: One kind does not concern the truths of Islam directly, and the other kind fights against the truths of belief.

questions.question: How is the first of those two main kinds described?
questions.answer: It is a false private belief and an unfair decision.

questions.question: What does the passage tell us about our focus on that first kind?
questions.answer: It says that kind is not the one being dealt with here.

questions.question: What is the first variety of the second main kind?
questions.answer: It is failing to accept the truth.

questions.question: Is that first variety presented as stubborn judgment or simple ignorance?
questions.answer: It is presented as simple ignorance.

questions.question: What is the second variety of the second main kind?
questions.answer: It is choosing in the heart to accept non-existence.

questions.question: Why is that second variety more serious than simple non-acceptance?
questions.answer: Because it includes a judgment and a side that the person takes.

questions.question: Into how many types is negation divided afterward?
questions.answer: It is divided into two types.

questions.question: What does the first type of negation deny?
questions.answer: It denies that something is present in a certain place or direction.

questions.question: Is that first type inside or outside the main discussion?
questions.answer: It is outside the main discussion.

questions.question: What subjects are included in the second type of negation?
questions.answer: It includes beliefs about this world, all creatures, the hereafter, and different times.

questions.question: What would someone need in order to prove that wide kind of denial?
questions.answer: They would need complete sight over the universe, the next life, and all time.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is unbelief mainly built on?
questions.answer: It is mainly built on denial, lack of knowledge, and rejection.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is belief mainly built on?
questions.answer: It is built on knowledge, confirmation, and sound judgment.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about the “negative” side of belief?
questions.answer: It teaches that behind it there is still a real truth.

questions.question: If someone tries very hard to make a denial into a settled belief, how is that described?
questions.answer: It is described as a mistaken and false kind of judgment.

questions.question: What is the passage’s view of mere refusal to accept the truth?
questions.answer: It views it as plain ignorance without a real judgment.

questions.question: What does “absolute ignorance” mean here in simple words?
questions.answer: It means not truly knowing and not making a sound decision.

questions.question: How many broad groups of unbelieving convictions are mentioned?
questions.answer: Two broad groups are mentioned.

questions.question: What is special about the first broad group?
questions.answer: It has its own false belief but is not directly the subject being argued about here.

questions.question: What action marks the second broad group?
questions.answer: It opposes the truths of faith.

questions.question: What is the first branch under that second group?
questions.answer: It is not agreeing with the truth.

questions.question: Why is this first branch called a kind of ignorance?
questions.answer: Because it does not reach the level of a formed judgment.

questions.question: What is the second branch under the second group?
questions.answer: It is inwardly approving non-existence.

questions.question: What extra step does this second branch have that the first branch does not?
questions.answer: It includes a heart-level choice and a judgment.

questions.question: Why does that heart-level choice matter?
questions.answer: Because once a person takes that side, he tries to defend the denial.

questions.question: What is one example of a denial that can be proven?
questions.answer: Denying that something is in one exact place or one exact direction.

questions.question: Why is that limited denial easier to prove?
questions.answer: Because it deals with one specific case instead of everything.

questions.question: Why is broad denial of religious truths impossible to prove from the passage’s point of view?
questions.answer: Because no one can inspect all beings, the next life, and all times completely.

questions.question: What main lesson about large religious denials can a student take from this passage?
questions.answer: Big denials are not easy claims to prove, because they would require impossible total knowledge.

questions.question: What three words best summarize unbelief in the passage?
questions.answer: Rejection, ignorance, and negation.

questions.question: What three ideas best summarize belief in the passage?
questions.answer: Knowledge, affirmation, and judgment.

questions.question: Does the passage treat unbelief as full and solid being, or as a kind of emptiness?
questions.answer: It treats it as a kind of emptiness.

questions.question: What does the passage mean when it says a denying part of belief can act like a gate?
questions.answer: It means that behind what looks negative, there is a real truth to be reached.

questions.question: In what case can a negative creed be looked at as a wrong kind of knowledge?
questions.answer: When someone turns denial into a settled acceptance of what is not real.

questions.question: What is the easier path in unbelief mentioned here?
questions.answer: Simply not accepting the truth.

questions.question: Why is simple non-acceptance weaker than a formed belief?
questions.answer: Because it does not even include a real judgment.

questions.question: What is the first of the two main kinds of unbelief?
questions.answer: A false and unfair belief that does not directly address the truths of Islam.

questions.question: What is the relationship of that first kind to the discussion?
questions.answer: It is left outside the main discussion.

questions.question: What is the second of the two main kinds of unbelief?
questions.answer: The kind that resists the truths of belief.

questions.question: What are the two varieties inside that resisting kind?
questions.answer: One is not accepting, and the other is accepting non-existence.

questions.question: Which variety is more than ignorance and becomes a chosen position?
questions.answer: Accepting non-existence is the chosen position.

questions.question: What makes that chosen position a matter of partiality?
questions.answer: The person’s heart takes the side of denial.

questions.question: What happens once someone takes the side of denial?
questions.answer: He feels the need to support and confirm that denial.

questions.question: What is the first type of negation discussed after that?
questions.answer: A denial about one specific location or direction.

questions.question: Why is this first type not the main concern here?
questions.answer: Because it can actually be demonstrated and is not the kind being challenged.

questions.question: What does the second type of negation try to deny?
questions.answer: It tries to deny wide truths about existence, the hereafter, and all ages.

questions.question: What kind of ability would be needed to prove such a huge denial?
questions.answer: A limitless view covering the whole universe, the next life, and every time period.

questions.question: If a student had to give the main idea of the passage in one sentence, what would it be?
questions.answer: The passage explains that belief is based on real knowledge, while the unbelief that fights faith is mostly denial and cannot truly prove its biggest claims.

questions.question: How does the passage describe belief in a positive way?
questions.answer: It describes belief as something real, knowing, and confirming.

questions.question: How does the passage describe unbelief in a negative way?
questions.answer: It describes unbelief as rejecting, not knowing, and leaning toward non-existence.

questions.question: Why might some unbelief seem stronger than it really is?
questions.answer: Because it may look like a firm claim even though it is built on denial.

questions.question: When does the passage allow unbelief to be called a mistaken kind of knowledge?
questions.answer: When a person actively accepts and approves a false negative view.

questions.question: What is called total ignorance in the passage?
questions.answer: Refusing to accept, while having no real judgment.

questions.question: What are the two large categories of convictions tied to unbelief?
questions.answer: One keeps its own false ideas without directly dealing with Islamic truths, and the other directly opposes faith.

questions.question: Why is the first category set aside?
questions.answer: Because the passage says it is not the matter under discussion.

questions.question: What makes the second category important in this passage?
questions.answer: It is the category that fights against the truths of belief.

questions.question: What is the first form inside this second category?
questions.answer: It is simply not agreeing with affirmation.

questions.question: What shows that this first form is not a full position?
questions.answer: It lacks a settled judgment.

questions.question: What is the second form inside this second category?
questions.answer: It is accepting non-existence in the heart.

questions.question: How is that second form different from simple non-acceptance?
questions.answer: It is a committed judgment rather than just a lack of acceptance.

questions.question: Why does commitment to denial lead to trying to affirm it?
questions.answer: Because once someone sides with it, he tries to uphold his chosen view.

questions.question: What is one narrow kind of denial that can be established?
questions.answer: Saying something is not in one certain place or direction.

questions.question: What broad kind of denial cannot be established?
questions.answer: Denying major sacred truths about all existence, the hereafter, and the ages.

questions.question: What reason is given for that broad denial being impossible to prove?
questions.answer: A person would need unlimited observation of all creation and all time.

questions.question: What caution does this passage teach about bold denials in religion?
questions.answer: It teaches that very wide denials should not be trusted, because they ask for proof no human can gather.

questions.question: What is the opening claim of the passage about unbelief that resists Islam?
questions.answer: Its real nature is denial, ignorance, and negation.

questions.question: What opposite qualities are given for belief?
questions.answer: Belief has knowledge, affirmation, and judgment.

questions.question: Why does the passage say unbelief may only appear to be something positive?
questions.answer: Because it can look like a claim, but underneath it is still a rejection.

questions.question: What can be hidden behind what seems like a negative side of belief?
questions.answer: A true and positive reality can be behind it.

questions.question: Under what condition is unbelief counted as a mistaken judgment rather than just ignorance?
questions.answer: When it becomes an accepted false conviction instead of mere refusal.

questions.question: What is meant by non-acceptance in this passage?
questions.answer: It means not agreeing with the truth without forming a true judgment.

questions.question: Why is non-acceptance said to be easy?
questions.answer: Because doing nothing but refusing is easier than proving and building a case.

questions.question: What is the first kind of unbelieving conviction named after the summary?
questions.answer: A false belief that does not pay attention to the truths of Islam.

questions.question: How does the passage treat that first kind in relation to the main topic?
questions.answer: It says that kind is not our concern here.

questions.question: What is the second kind of unbelieving conviction?
questions.answer: The kind that pushes against the truths of belief.

questions.question: What are its two varieties?
questions.answer: One is non-acceptance, and the other is accepting non-existence.

questions.question: Which variety includes the heart taking a side?
questions.answer: Accepting non-existence includes the heart taking a side.

questions.question: What does that heart-side-taking lead a person to do?
questions.answer: It leads him to defend his denial as if it were true.

questions.question: What is the first type of negation listed after these varieties?
questions.answer: Denying the presence of something in a specific place or direction.

questions.question: What makes this first type manageable to prove?
questions.answer: It is limited to one defined case.

questions.question: What does the second type of negation cover?
questions.answer: It covers wide sacred teachings about the universe, beings, the hereafter, and the flow of ages.

questions.question: Why does the passage say this second type cannot be supported?
questions.answer: Because proving it would require total knowledge beyond human reach.

questions.question: What deep understanding should a careful reader gain from the ending of the passage?
questions.answer: A careful reader should understand that broad denial of faith is a huge claim that cannot be truly backed up.
